items.title: Karnataka cancels 16 licences, suspends 8 over spurious drugs: Full list
items.summary: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration (FSDA) has cancelled the licences of 16 pharmaceutical retailers and wholesalers, and suspended those of eight others, including Pfizer Ltd’s wholesale depot in Nelamangala, as part of an ongoing investigation into the alleged distribution and sale of spurious drugs. The action follows the FSDA’s August 18 raid on a farmhouse in Bidadi, in Bengaluru South district, where the department said it uncovered an unlicensed drug repacking and relabelling operation. Drugs, injection-filling machinery, forged labels and stamps and other material worth Rs 5.05 crore were seized from the premises. As part of the follow-up investigation, the FSDA said it cancelled 16 drug licences and suspended eight others belonging to retailers and wholesalers involved in the alleged distribution and sale of the spurious medicines. The licence of Pfizer Ltd’s wholesale depot at Kempanalinganahalli in Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural district, has also been suspended. The 16 cancelled licences include those of Avesco Healthcare, Bangalore Speciality Pharma, Bengalurus Speciality Pharma, Patel Medi Trade, Rajarajeshwari Pharma, N.S. Pharma, Surya Speciality

items.title: Supreme Court orders Allahabad HC to defer case over Rahul Gandhi's assets; directs CBI to halt report
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday ordered the Allahabad High Court to defer proceedings before it in a petition filed by a BJP worker alleging that Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi possesses assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana also ordered the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or any other authority not to submit any report to the High Court in the meantime. During the hearing, the Court asked why the High Court passed orders in the case without giving Gandhi an opportunity of hearing. "Suppose somebody commits murders, etc. police does not need permission. But what appears to us is, subject to the assistance provided to us from both sides, if the Court wants to issue a direction, the courts are expected to follow the principle of natural justice," the CJI remarked. The Bench also said that if any agency has knowledge of any disproportionate assets belonging to any individual, it can proceed on its own and the same does not require court orders. items.title: Suspended directors have to give confidentiality undertaking for access to resolution plan: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has held that a resolution professional can ask suspended directors to furnish a confidentiality undertaking before providing them access to a resolution plan and other confidential material in a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) [Mandava Prabhakar Rao Vs Navneet Gupta]. Technical Member Naresh Salecha , who was called upon to resolve an earlier split verdict by the NCLAT, agreed with the view that such a requirement does not violate the rights of suspended directors to participate CIRP. “ The resolution professional can take an undertaking from members of the erstwhile board of directors to maintain confidentiality, ” Salecha held. He said that the right of suspended directors to access resolution plans has to operate alongside their obligation to maintain confidentiality. The ruling arose from appeals filed by Mandava Prabhakar Rao, a suspended director of NSL Nagapatnam Power and Infratech Limited. The dispute concerned the company's 20th Committee of Creditors (CoC) meeting held on July 16, 2024. Rao had nominated Nelluri Bapuji to represent the suspended management in CoC meetings. items.title: Cops Kanthi Rana, Vishal Gunni accused in Kadambari Jethwani case given new postings
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Two years after their suspension in the infamous Kadambari Jethwani case, the Andhra Pradesh government on Sunday, September 20, transferred and assigned new postings for former Vijayawada Commissioner Kanthi Rana Tata and Deputy Commissioner Vishal Gunni. The government issued orders posting Kanthi Rana as the Traffic Management and Road Safety’s Inspector General of Police. Vishal Gunni was posted as Deputy Inspector General of Police, Training, in the existing vacancy, and given full additional charge as Director of the Andhra Pradesh Police Academy (APPA) until further orders. The postings come two weeks after the Andhra government, on September 4, revoked their suspension. While revoking their suspension, the state government said that the decision was based on reports from the Director General of Police (DGP) and the Head of Police Force (HoPF). The two cops were accused of illegally confining and harassing Mumbai based actress Kadambari Jethwani and her family. items.title: Karnataka minister says ‘nothing wrong’ in tipping officials, sparks row
items.summary: Karnataka Excise Minister and Hassan district in-charge minister KM Shivalinge Gowda triggered a controversy on Saturday, September 19, after he said citizens could “respectfully” offer money to government officials who complete their work on time. Gowda made the remarks while addressing a ‘Praja Seva Andolana’ public grievance meeting in Sakleshpur, Hassan district. He was responding to a query from a member of the public when he said, “Whatever you want to offer, you can do so respectfully. It is your dharma, but nobody should take money forcibly.” When some people in the audience asked what they should offer “respectfully”, the minister reportedly said it was left to them. The minister had also said there was “nothing wrong” if citizens willingly gave ‘tips’ or an ‘honorarium’ to government officials for getting their work done on time. The remarks drew objections from people at the meeting. Punit, a farmer from Alur who was present with a land-related grievance, questioned the minister’s statement. “Officials are paid a salary. BAPS: The Hindu organisation at the heart of Modi’s cultural diplomacy
items.summary: “Strike and closure of the Eiffel Tower after the expulsion of female staff during a visit by a Hindu delegation” This was what a prominent French newspaper said on September 7 this year. The Hindu delegation belonged to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or the BAPS, and it made global headlines. But the interesting question is not just what happened in Paris. It is this: how did a religious organisation with deeply conservative internal rules become one of the most powerful global faces of Indian culture? BAPS has spectacular temples, a wealthy and influential global following, a vast charity network and an extraordinary relationship with Narendra Modi. It also has a much more complicated history involving women, caste, labour and political power. So who exactly is BAPS? And why has the Indian state invested so heavily in projecting it worldwide?
